checks: Matched 870e8284d5328056 §§1–3, (1)–(9). Containment is the lower offset bound for each plane. Clipping a larger offset to the corresponding support of P preserves the set. Interior integer membership would persist near a limiting parameter by strict inequalities, so the feasible parameter set is closed. Compactness of P gives the outer-neighborhood volume upper bound, including a lower-dimensional limit.

At a genuine cut plane, the relative-interior facet is contained in the relative interior of the section of P by that plane, hence is inside int P. A small outward motion gives positive volume by a prism over a relative ball. For the finite lattice census, a point on ∂P or another unchanged cut cannot enter the interior, and any strict violation of the moved owner persists for sufficiently small motion. This forces a relative-interior lattice witness. Its own strict slack on the other distinct cuts also proves failure of the simultaneous outward motion.

Verified Gauss–Green entrywise: the divergence of (z_k−q_k)e_j is δ_jk and the boundary term is n_j(z_k−q_k). The scalar witness replaces only the normal coordinate of the facet centroid. The support distance on Γ_P is bounded below by the radius of an interior ball of L at q.

Verified the signed strip derivative by expanding (I+tB)^{-1} at a genuine plane. Its signed motion in the original normal coordinate is t a_i·(Bw+v)+O(t²) uniformly on a bounded strip. Pairwise distinct planes and the relative boundary of the section of P give surface-null exceptional sets. Telescoping the planes and dominated convergence cover both signs of time. A coincident inherited plane stays fixed and contributes only to Γ_P, and identical active inequalities use one owner.

overlap.comparison: Attains a fixed-projection depth optimization under conditions on compatible varying continuous fibers and bounded facet data. Here P is fixed and ordinary base volume is optimized by a finite offset vector.
Uses an interior fiber for normalization and attainment on a fixed integer base. It does not give the offset optimum, lattice facet witnesses, or inherited boundary flux.

The projected facets are from an auxiliary lattice-disjoint container and the budgets concern strict exteriors. This result fixes an actual outer body and allows lattice points on the inherited and cut boundaries.

readability: Read genuine facets as facets on cutting planes meeting int P, with coincident copies grouped before the strip argument. The proof makes this convention and the fixed status of inherited supports explicit.
review_method: Independent cold proof read, source and dependency comparison, and exact calculation
summary: The fixed-direction maximum and both boundary variations are proved. A positive-area inherited piece remains in the boundary flux, and each genuine cut at the positive-volume optimum has an actual lattice witness in its relative interior.
